icds.title: Analog acquisition module, classic CAN 500 kbit/s
GNSS timing receiver, serial time messages and pulse per second
IEEE 1588 precision time protocol, two-step, end-to-end
Data acquisition unit telemetry and diagnostics, UDP/IPv4

requirements.title: Wire formats follow the ICDs
requirements.text: Every message is encoded and decoded with the field order, sizes and byte order of its ICD.

requirements.title: Lengths are exact
requirements.text: A payload whose length is not the one its ICD defines (including an array whose count does not match) is rejected.

requirements.title: Out-of-range values are not used
requirements.text: Values outside their ICD range are rejected and counted before any reading is produced from them.

requirements.title: Frames survive any chunking
requirements.text: The serial deframer delivers every valid frame whatever the size and boundaries of the reads.

requirements.title: Resynchronisation after corruption
requirements.text: A corrupted frame costs at most that frame; the next valid frame is delivered, including when the corrupt bytes contain a sync word.

requirements.title: CRC errors are counted
requirements.text: Each frame with a CRC error is counted and reported in diagnostics.

requirements.title: Impossible lengths do not stall a link
requirements.text: A length longer than the device can send is treated as corruption at once.

requirements.title: IMU samples carry acquisition time
requirements.text: IMU samples are stamped with the time they were taken (device time mapped to local time by a running minimum of arrival minus device time), so transport jitter does not move time stamps by more than 30 us.

requirements.title: Lost IMU samples are counted
requirements.text: Gaps in the 16-bit sample counter are counted across its wrap; gaps longer than imu.max_gap_samples are logged as faults.

requirements.title: Device time wraps
requirements.text: The 32-bit microsecond device time is unwrapped so time stamps stay continuous across its wrap.

requirements.title: IMU start-up and supervision
requirements.text: The unit commands an IMU self-test and then streaming, repeats both every second while no samples arrive, logs a lost IMU, and reports the IMU healthy only after a passed self-test with samples arriving.

requirements.title: Module supervision
requirements.text: A module without heartbeat for aam.heartbeat_timeout_ms is reported lost, logged once, and fails the module built-in test; a module the armed plan uses is supervised from arming, even if it has never sent a heartbeat.

requirements.title: Lost data frames are detected per group
requirements.text: Each data group's frame counter is checked separately; a missing frame is counted and logged.

requirements.title: Engineering values and over-range
requirements.text: Counts are converted with the channel's range, scale and offset; a count at full scale is flagged over-range.

requirements.title: Plans are parsed strictly
requirements.text: Unknown statements or keys, duplicate keys, malformed numbers and missing required keys reject the plan (PLN-01, PLN-02).

requirements.title: Channel names and count
requirements.text: Channel names are unique and 1-16 of a-z, 0-9, _; a plan has 1..plan.max_channels channels (PLN-03, PLN-04).

requirements.title: Sources exist
requirements.text: Every channel names a module 1..32 and input that exists, or an IMU field that exists (PLN-05).

requirements.title: Rates are achievable
requirements.text: Module rates are the base rate over an allowed divisor; IMU rates are one of plan.allowed_imu_rates_hz (PLN-06).

requirements.title: Ranges and filters exist
requirements.text: Every range and filter is one the module offers (PLN-07).

requirements.title: Inputs in one data frame share a rate
requirements.text: Inputs carried in the same data frame must be planned at the same rate (PLN-08).

requirements.title: An input is used once
requirements.text: No physical input or IMU field appears in two channels (PLN-09).

requirements.title: Alarm limits are measurable
requirements.text: Alarm limits are ordered and inside what the channel can measure given its range, scale and offset; scale is not zero (PLN-10, PLN-13).

requirements.title: CAN bus load
requirements.text: The plan's worst-case CAN bus load, with bit stuffing, does not exceed plan.max_can_bus_load (PLN-11).

requirements.title: Telemetry link budget
requirements.text: The plan's telemetry bit rate, with packet and network overhead, does not exceed plan.telemetry_link_bps (PLN-12).

requirements.title: Register writes are acknowledged
requirements.text: Every register request is answered within plan.reg_timeout_ms or retried, at most plan.reg_retries times; then the load fails.

requirements.title: Aborts fail the load
requirements.text: A module abort fails the load at once with the module's abort code.

requirements.title: Configuration is read back
requirements.text: After commit every written register is read back and compared; a mismatch fails the load. All inputs of a used module are written.

requirements.title: Module configuration CRC
requirements.text: Each module's configuration CRC must equal the CRC computed from the plan; otherwise the load fails and is logged.

requirements.title: Telemetry only under an armed plan
requirements.text: No telemetry is sent until a plan is loaded and verified; every packet carries the CRC of the plan in force; a rejected plan leaves the armed one in force.

requirements.title: Late answers are not misattributed
requirements.text: An answer to an earlier request is never taken as the answer to the current one.

requirements.title: PTP exchange
requirements.text: Offset and path delay are computed from the two-step end-to-end exchange; Follow_Up and Delay_Resp are matched by sequence id and requester identity; other domains and versions are ignored. The PTP servo removes a constant oscillator error.

requirements.title: Delay outliers
requirements.text: An exchange whose path delay exceeds timing.ptp_outlier_factor times the running minimum does not adjust the clock.

requirements.title: GNSS time is checked
requirements.text: A GNSS time message is used only with valid time and leap flags, a 2D or 3D fix, accuracy within timing.gnss_max_acc_ns, and within timing.gnss_max_msg_delay_ms of its PPS edge; each edge is used once.

requirements.title: Slew, do not step
requirements.text: Offsets up to 1 ms are removed by adjusting the clock rate, so time never runs backwards; larger offsets step the clock and are logged.

requirements.title: Lock
requirements.text: Lock is declared after timing.lock_count consecutive measurements within the active source's lock threshold and lost on one beyond its unlock threshold.

requirements.title: Holdover and free-running
requirements.text: Without measurements for timing.holdover_start_ms the unit enters holdover at the learned rate (quality 1); after timing.holdover_max_ms it is free-running (quality 0).

requirements.title: Source selection
requirements.text: Sources are used in timing.sources priority; the unit fails over at once when the active source is lost and returns to a better one only after it has been good for timing.switch_hold_ms.

requirements.title: Time-stamp accuracy end to end
requirements.text: While locked to PTP on the bench, 99 % of module samples are stamped within 1 ms of true time.

requirements.title: Packet integrity
requirements.text: Every telemetry packet ends with a CRC-32 over the packet and carries a sequence number one above the previous one.

requirements.title: Sample order and offsets
requirements.text: Samples in a packet are in acquisition order, with non-negative offsets from the packet time; every sample sent is counted.

requirements.title: Alarm flags
requirements.text: A sample below its alarm low limit carries alarm_low, above its high limit alarm_high.

requirements.title: IMU decimation
requirements.text: IMU channels are decimated from 400 Hz to their planned rate.

requirements.title: Status
requirements.text: A status request returns uptime, software version, boot slot, built-in test, time state and source, offset, link counters and the plan CRC.

requirements.title: Bounded fault log
requirements.text: The fault log holds diag.fault_log_capacity records; repeats within one second are folded; when full the oldest is overwritten and counted.

requirements.title: Malformed requests
requirements.text: A malformed diagnostic request is logged and not answered.

requirements.title: Signed packages only
requirements.text: A package is accepted only if its Ed25519 signature over the header verifies against the release key and the image matches the signed hash; nothing is written otherwise.

requirements.title: Hardware match
requirements.text: A package built for other hardware (unit.hw_id) is refused.

requirements.title: Anti-rollback
requirements.text: A package below the security floor is refused; the floor rises only when a new image is confirmed.

requirements.title: Inactive slot only
requirements.text: Install writes only the inactive slot and reads it back before marking it pending.

requirements.title: Trial boot
requirements.text: A pending image gets update.max_trial_boots boots; unless confirmed by the application it is rolled back.

requirements.title: Verified boot
requirements.text: The boot selector verifies the image it is about to boot; a damaged active image falls back to a verified other slot, and with none the unit does not boot.

requirements.title: Power loss during update
requirements.text: Losing power at any write leaves a bootable, verified image.

requirements.title: Exact replay
requirements.text: Replaying a recording of the unit's inputs reproduces its telemetry byte for byte.

requirements.title: Fault campaign
requirements.text: Under the bench fault campaign (bit errors, dropped and out-of-range samples, a lost module, a GNSS outage, PTP outage and jitter, module register faults) the unit keeps running, reports each fault, and sends no packet with a bad CRC.

requirements.title: Reproducible build
requirements.text: Two builds of the same sources with the same toolchain in different directories produce identical binaries.

requirements.title: Hardened binaries
requirements.text: Shipped binaries are position independent, with full RELRO, a non-executable stack, stack protection and CET.

requirements.title: Static analysis clean
requirements.text: clang-tidy and cppcheck report no findings in shipped code; sanitizer builds pass every unit test.

requirements.title: Release evidence
requirements.text: Every release carries its SBOM, the test evidence, the traceability matrix and a configuration manifest, all hashed and signed.
